correctness.rationale: Set x=√z1,y=√z2,u=x+y,b=λ−λ^-1,a=λ+λ^-1. The symmetric branch has unique positive root since 2x+x^-1−x^-2 is strictly increasing. For x≠y, direct add/subtract of original fixed-point equations gives Qλ(u)=u²−au+(λ−1)/(λ+1)=0 and (x−y)²=2bu−u²−2. The lower positive Q root always yields negative square, while upper root switches sign only at the unique positive zero of p=4λ⁴+7λ³−14λ²−33λ−12 (Descartes plus exact signs). Independent high precision roots give λc=2.10281584329; direct substitution of x,y for λ=2.11 and 3 reproduces the original equations to roundoff and yields two swapped nonsymmetric solutions; λ=2.10 has none. No claim about general Gibbs measures.
